environment.description: AWS ECS Fargate service consuming from SQS queue. PostgreSQL 15 on RDS with row-level security policies. The database connection uses role 'app_tenant_consumer' which has FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY applied via ALTER TABLE tenant_records FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY. The RLS policy is defined as: CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation ON tenant_records USING (tenant_id = current_setting('app.current_tenant')::uuid) WITH CHECK (tenant_id = current_setting('app.current_tenant')::uuid). The role is NOT a superuser and does not have BYPASSRLS privilege. Note: the JWT algorithm confusion vulnerability still exists and tokens can still be forged, but the forged tenant_id in the JWT is used to SET app.current_tenant which then constrains all queries through the RLS policy to only return/modify rows belonging to that tenant_id. The attacker can impersonate any tenant but can only access data belonging to the tenant they claim to be.

config.database: PostgreSQL 15 on RDS, role: app_tenant_consumer (no BYPASSRLS), FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY on tenant_records, policy: tenant_id = current_setting('app.current_tenant')::uuid
config.queue: SQS Standard queue, no message attribute filtering
config.network: VPC with private subnets, NAT gateway egress only
config.key_distribution: RSA public key in /app/config/public.pem, also served at /.well-known/jwks.json
config.additional_note: RLS policy enforcement is at the PostgreSQL engine level independent of application logic
